leadIn.title: Lead-In & Context: Quantifiers
leadIn.content: Talking about amounts: We have a lot of apples, some milk, but no eggs in the fridge.

meaningCheck.question: "Quantifiers" — Does the condition describe a real possibility or a hypothetical imaginary scenario?
options: It sets up a specific condition and its communicative result
It describes a guaranteed past fact that cannot change
It is only used for giving formal orders
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Conditionals express dependent conditions and their logical outcomes.

meaningCheck.question: Structural check: In conditional sentences, can the 'if' clause come second?
options: No, the 'if' clause must always be the first two words
Yes, clause order can flip without changing the fundamental condition
meaningCheck.explanation: Correct · Clause position can reverse; a comma is used when 'if' starts the sentence.

form.title: Form & Structure: Quantifiers
form.content: Quantifiers + Noun: a lot of (large amount), some (medium amount), a few / a little (small amount), no / none (zero).
